reason: Prioritize int3-g64 as the direct group-size test for improving 3-bit quality, with lower expected weight memory than int4; smaller groups may improve quantization quality but can add metadata and reduce throughput. mixed3-4-g64 tests smaller groups while protecting selected modules; int3-g32 is a stronger metadata and throughput risk. Existing evidence shows int3-g128 at 0.80 quality and mixed3-4-g128 at 0.85, so none is known to meet the 0.95 quality and throughput gates. These are hypotheses; the two trials should focus on useful memory reduction with a chance of clearing quality, while retaining int4-g128 as the measured quality-safe reference.
